name: Granny Smith Apple
lede: Granny Smith Apple is a pale, yellowish green named for the apple variety, barely present in our painting archive.

sections.title: Named for the apple, not further explained
sections.body: Granny Smith Apple takes its name from the green apple variety [1]. Wikipedia's color list is our only source for the name, and it does not document who first used the apple's color as a color name [1]. Its nearest named look-alikes in our library are [[greenish-hospital-green]], [[light-grey-green]], [[hospital-green]] and [[very-light-green]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green in just one of the 23,781 paintings we have, a work attributed to Alexander von Kotzebue and dated 1857, as photographed [2]. That is a trace presence, not a pattern, and this archive describes our own museum holdings, not painting as a whole [2]. The hex value, #A8E4A0, is a pale, yellowish green typical of the apple's skin rather than its flesh, and is a screen approximation like every value in our library [1].
